rule: Every health statement carries a grade AND names its test article: whole_herb | named_extract (with solvent and standardisation where known) | essential_oil | isolated_compound | multi_herb_formula. A grade belongs to the test article, never to the plant, the tea or a single constituent unless that is what was tested. A D or E finding is never phrased as an effect in people; a T grade says "traditionally used for", never "helps" or "treats".

grades.basis: systematic review or meta-analysis of human randomised controlled trials
at least one human randomised controlled trial
human observational or small uncontrolled studies (open-label, case series); a meta-analysis of observational studies is C, not A
traditional use documented in an official monograph (EMA HMPC, ESCOP, WHO, Commission E)

example: Enteric-coated peppermint oil for IBS symptoms is grade A for that oil in capsules [54]; it is not evidence for menthol alone and not evidence for peppermint tea [6,129].
